ms.report:
What we promised:
Orcfax will identify auditing firms to review both on-chain and off-chain components of the Orcfax solution. Once identified, Orcfax will finalize a Contract for Services with the selected auditing firms, announce these contracts via social media (Discord, X), and provide links to access the contracts.

What we delivered:
Upon approval of the original SoM in 2024 Orcfax requested quotes from several auditing firms for the work required to review both Orcfax on-chain and off-chain components; these firms were evaluated based on their portfolios of work within the Cardano ecosystem, cost, and availability given our Catalyst timeline. A contract with TxPipe was negotiated for auditing on-chain components, and a contract with BlinkLabs was negotiated for the off-chain components.
On 08/27/2024 Orcfax announced on X that a contract with TxPipe had been finalized. We shared this same information on Discord. A screenshot of the announcement is included in docs (linked at the end) .
On 09/29/2024 Orcfax announced on X that a contract with BlinkLabs had been finalized. The following day, on 09/30/2024, we announced this contract on Discord. A screenshot of the announcement included in docs.
Both contracts have been made available on our docs site.

ms.report:
What we promised:
Orcfax will release an interim report on audit status with strategy for addressing any auditor feedback/additional requests; this information will be made available in Orcfax docs and public Github repository.
What we delivered:
After contract finalization, auditors were given access to Orcfax systems. The following constitutes the feedback received from each and the Orcfax strategy for addressing auditor feedback/additional requests. These details and links to relevant deliverables have also been made available on our public GitHub docs.
The on-chain audit
TxPipe provided the following interim report
After review of the report, the Orcfax team acknowledged the identified info-level finding (ORC-301). However, as this does not constitute an “issue” (per TxPipe definitions) with the on-chain code, Orcfax has decided not to resolve the finding at this time. It is our opinion that this is, at worst, a tooling concern.
"INFO" as defined by TxPipe
Info are not issues. These are just pieces of information that are beneficial to the dApp creator. These are not necessarily acted on or have a resolution, they are logged for the completeness of the audit. (Audit Report, 18)
The finding can be simplified as follows: When using a chain indexer, if an integrator filters on address, they may miss utxos that have different stake credentials. This is correct.
However, integrators can just as easily filter on the payment credential, which is the preferred method as this ensures the use of a valid FS as publication is permissionless. Additionally, integrator’s are informed as to where the FS will be published; a deviation from this address on the part of Orcfax is unlikely and would be communicated with integrators in advance if deemed necessary for any reason.

What we delivered:
After acknowledging initial feedback and providing the additional access described in the previous milestone, the auditors continued their work. The following constitutes the feedback received from each and the Orcfax strategy for addressing auditor feedback/additional requests. These details and links to relevant deliverables have also been made available on our public GitHub docs.

The on-chain audit
TxPipe provided the following final report
The report lists four Info-level (i.e. advisory) findings which the Orcfax team has acknowledged. However, as these do not constitute issues with the on-chain code, Orcfax has decided not to resolve them at this time. This decision has been made because resolution would result in a disruption of service for integrators, and the potential improvements are outweighed by the possible cost of remediation (e.g. the possibility of making new mistakes by renaming or refactoring code); if or when an update to the Orcfax on-chain service is needed, this decision will be reevaluated. This business decision balances reliability and responsibility given that these info-level findings in some cases constitute, at worst, tooling concerns.
The four info level findings are explained in the report and Orcfax has provided simplified explanations in the above linked docs.

The off-chain audit
In accordance with the delivery schedule outlined in the last milestone, Orcfax provided BlinkLabs with the first batch of records to demonstrate infrastructure adherence to SOC2 standards. A link to the requested evidence can be found here.

If any non-critical recommendations have been made, Orcfax will provide a response as to whether and when such recommendations will be addressed.

The on-chain audit
TxPipe provided their final report in milestone three; Orcfax provided a response and rationale for the four Info-level (i.e. advisory) findings listed in the report.

The off-chain audit
In accordance with the delivery schedule outlined in milestone 2, Orcfax has incrementally provided BlinkLabs with the requested materials for audit. Since the last milestone, Orcfax has provided the third and final batch of records to demonstrate infrastructure adherence to SOC2 standards. A link to the requested evidence can be found here.
This work has culminated in a system description, which can be accessed here.
The evidence submitted has been accepted by BlinkLabs as satisfactory. A letter evidencing the completion of the final batch has been included in the public GitHub docs.

An announcement regarding this successful completion of the audits has also been published to X

List of challenge KPIs and how the project addressed them
・Confirm solution maturity: Orcfax underwent an audit (TxPipe) of its on-chain components in order to prove out the maturity of its on-chain solution to integrators, and received a final report with zero issues.
・Enhance system security: Orcfax underwent an audit (BlinkLabs) of its off-chain architecture and business processes in order to demonstrate to its stakeholders that the project is committed to building mature infrastructure governed by security best practices; the result of this audit was improved governing policy and an exhaustive systems description.
・Provide a model for infrastructure audits on Cardano: While there are aspects of this process that our team would improve upon if done again, we do still believe that Orcfax has demonstrated how other projects on Cardano could propose and execute audits of their projects– especially if their projects is an ecosystem service and/or is open-source.
・What could have been improved: Additional research into audit processes prior to applying for catalyst monies would have been prudent as it likely would have prevented lengthy project delays which were the result of our ignorance relating to how audits are executed; after contracting our auditing firms, Orcfax needed to submit change requests to reshape the catalyst grant in order to fit audit processes.
